 HONOLULU – The University of Hawaii men's basketball team used a strong second-half performance to dispatch UT Arlington 71-62 on the second night of the 60th Annual OUTRIGGER Rainbow Classic Sunday at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center. 
With their third straight victory to start the season, the Rainbow Warriors (3-0) moved one step closer to capturing the program's 18th overall Rainbow Classic title. The 'Bows look for a tournament three-peat when they take on Portland on Monday night at 7:00 p.m. 
UH has now won eight straight Rainbow Classic games, dating back to 2024.
Frontcourt players Zack Davidson and Bol Dengdit shook off early foul trouble to lead UH's second-half charge. Davidson led UH in scoring for the second straight game, finishing with 21 points on 8-of-13 shooting from the field and 5-of-6 from the free-throw line. Dengdit finished with 15 points on 5-of-8 shooting.
Meanwhile, Jaden Matingou was a spark plug in the second half, scoring all but two of his 12 points after the break. Chance Trujillo also chipped in 12 points and a team-high four assists. Marcus Adams Jr. and Tanner Cuff tied for team-high honors with eight rebounds each.
After shooting 28.6 percent from the field in the first half, UH shot 48.4 percent in the second to surge away from the Mavericks (2-1).
 I 👀 you @ChanceTrujillo5 ➡️ @boldengdit7 📺 K5/MW+ #GoBows https://t.co/KQQ8nDRpeE
— HAWAII BASKETBALL (@HawaiiMBB) November 9, 2026 
The first half saw each team go through offensive struggles. UH got off to a fast start, scoring 11 of the first 13 points of the game and eventually taking a 19-6 lead on Adams' three-pointer at the 8:35 mark. It was a nightmare start for the Mavericks, who missed 13 of their first 14 shots and went without a field goal for nearly 10 minutes. 
But after Mier Panoam ended the drought with a driving layup at 7:36, the Mavericks flipped the script on the 'Bows, who went on a four-minute drought. A 10-0 run briefly gave UTA the lead late in the first half before the teams went into the locker room deadlocked, 27-27. UTA made eight of its final 10 field goal attempts of the half, while UH ended the half shooting just 29 percent from the floor after its strong start.    
UTA took its biggest lead of the game, 38-34, four minutes into the second half, and UH answered to tie it up at 40-40 on Trujillo's jumper at the 14:15 mark. After another tie at 45-45, Davidson accounted for 10 points in a 17-3 UH run, and the 'Bows opened up a 58-48 lead when Matingou completed a three-point play. The lead grew to 14 at 62-48 when Matingou scooped up an errant pass and went in for a dunk with 4:24 left.
 And ☝🏽 @JadenShloop 📺 K5/MW+ #GoBows https://t.co/tCC8vmrLKu
— HAWAII BASKETBALL (@HawaiiMBB) November 9, 2026 
UTA made a push to close to six at 64-58 with 1:23 remaining, but UH made seven of eight free throws to seal the win.
Tristan Hankins led UTA with a game-high 23 points and hit five three-pointers. UH held UTA to just 5-of-20 on three-point shooting in the second half. 
In the first game of the day, Portland cruised past Bethesda, 130-56.
The Rainbow Classic concludes on Monday with UT Arlington facing Bethesda at 4:30 p.m., followed by Hawaii vs. Portland at 7 p.m.
